In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
emotional intelligence is a set of skills that can be learned and that can help us to be better people and better leaders.
emotional intelligence is a complex construct that has been defined, measured and researched by different scholars in different ways, and that there is a lot to learn about it.

emotional intelligence (EI) is a set of abilities that enable a person to recognize his or her own emotions, and those of others, to discriminate between different emotions and to label them appropriately, and to use emotional information to guide thinking and behavior (Petrides, Furnham, 2001; Petrides, Furnham & Frederickson, 2004).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
emotional intelligence is a set of skills that helps individuals to understand their own and others' emotions, and to use this knowledge to manage emotions in themselves and others.

we are able to show that there are significant differences in the emotional intelligence of the two groups of participants, and that the differences in emotional intelligence are related to differences in the use of social skills.
we are able to show that the emotional intelligence concept is not a mere buzz word, but a real concept that can be measured and that has an impact on important work outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are two distinct types of emotional intelligence, and the two types are differentially related to different outcomes.
there is no such thing as a general intelligence factor.
